_doc: Default gitvow policy. Regex (Python re) on Bash command text, edited file paths, or MCP tool names. Order: deny → confirm → allow; unmatched calls are allowed and logged. Confirm rules take 'when': 'immediate' (Bash default) or 'commit' (path default; asked on one card when the agent commits). Copy to <repo>/.gitvow/policy.json or ~/.gitvow/policy.json to customise.

path_confirm.reason: edits gitvow's own policy, redaction rules or hooks
edits an authorization or gate-bearing file

decisions._doc: rule_threshold: consistent answers by authorities before a finding becomes an earned rule; rule_decay_days: days without a new confirmation before it lapses. mode: open (the agent's commit is stopped once with the card, then goes through with Gitvow-Open for every finding nobody answered; a person's commit goes through the same way) or strict (agent and person alike: refused until every finding has a gitvow decide answer). authorities: emails, email local parts or names whose decisions count; empty means anyone with commit access. session_scope: an immediate confirm is recorded as a finding and a person's yes (gitvow decide <n> accept --scope session, or the agent's own approve button) holds for the rest of the session; the next commit carries it as a scoped decision, which is never precedent. false: ask every time, record nothing.

llm_classifier._doc: Optional: a command that reads the hook JSON on stdin and prints ALLOW|CONFIRM|DENY <reason>. Used only for calls not matched above.

_doc_commands: A command rule is either {pattern} or {program, verbs}. The second form matches the program in command position (not inside another program's quoted argument) and allows options between the program and the verb (kubectl --context prod delete); write new command rules in that form. It may add 'target', a regex on what the command reaches, read from the environment before it runs: for kubectl and helm the context from --context/--kube-context or the kubeconfig's current-context, plus namespace; for git push the remote URL and branch; for terraform the workspace under -chdir. A target that cannot be read matches every target rule, so an action of unknown reach is asked about. Rules are tried in order, so put the target-specific tier first and the catch-all observe tier after it. Reads are never rules: kubectl get, aws s3 ls, SELECT. The database-write rule matches a client program on the line and a writing statement anywhere after it; grep for UPDATE in a source tree is not a write. decisions.indirect_commands (allow|observe|commit|immediate, default observe) is the tier for a command whose program the gate cannot read from the text: eval, source, a variable in program position, or a shell running a script file.
_doc_when: when: immediate stops the call and asks now; commit records a finding and asks on the card at commit; observe records the finding on the commit as Gitvow-Observed and asks nobody, ever. Observe costs zero interruptions, so it is the tier to put a pattern in when you want the record to show how often it happens before anyone decides whether it deserves a question.
